text:
Liam Ohgren has six goals in 22 games for Vancouver, two shy of the eight he scored in 69 games last season. The 2022 first-round pick (19th overall, by Minnesota) is getting chances at a better rate than last year, and his shot has real weight: his hardest this season ranks in the 87th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 53% of his shots coming off the rush.

Our numbers flag him as due to cool. He has scored on 21% of his shots against 9% last season, six goals on 3.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and his hot stretch reads mostly as bounces. The goals have already dried up: four came in a five-game burst in late October and early November, none in the six games since.

The bigger worry is five on five. Vancouver has taken just 37% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had him among the forwards whose teams created the least last season, partly because he played with weaker linemates. His minutes are down nearly two a night lately. Watch whether the chances keep coming once the shooting percentage settles.
